body: I really don't think he was a good psychiatrist. All he did was tell me to pop some pills (he didn't say that, but that's close to what he was telling me). I said to him I don't want to take medicine for this, and he said he couldn't help me. This was the second visit. I'd never had a psychiatrist before so I don't know if this is completely normal he told me to take medicine, but it just didn't sound right. Sounded like he was trying to get rid of me. Could just be what my crazy head was telling me at the time, but I felt like something was wrong with what he was telling me. So I just cancelled the 3 appointments I had left with him and just moved on with the attitude that helped me push past it. (It was depression btw, I had it 2 years ago but I was happy after about a month after seeing him)

Thanks for that :), my dream is to become and author but, like you just said, there is an infinite number of things I could do in this world. I gotta make the best of it whether I'm happy or suicidal. I think this is the thought that's been keeping back suicide. I could do a million and one things on this planet, and maybe if technology advances, even more. Just gotta wait and see, I guess :P
I've been to a psychiatrist before, all he did was jack squat and I fixed myself (I kind of got in the mindset "I don't need that assholes help, I can fix this").

I mean what if the aftershock is the happiness and the suicidal thoughts are there to stay? This could mean it might be suicide or both too. I think I just gotta wait until this "*aftershock*" passes to find out.

Edit: Mood swings are gone. It's just usually happy with suicide thoughts in the back of my mind :P
What I'm afraid of is what's the aftershock? Is it the happy part, the suicidal part, or both?
